projectDesc.p: This file defines analytical categories for conventional formulaic passages in Armenian colophons. It contains four speech-act classes and eighteen initial subcategories. The classification is ready for test encoding but remains open to evidenced revision. It records functions, nested standard patterns, and the individual Armenian occurrences supplied in the test colophons. Names, dates, places, and minor verbal variants do not automatically create new patterns.
The classification is held in taxonomy/category/catDesc within this file.

These source descriptions document the supplied readings without allocating central bibliography IDs. They may later be linked to verified records in listbibl.xml. The four parent classes follow Schiegg; the eighteen child categories are project definitions developed by Lewis Read, informed by these studies. They are not a verbatim taxonomy attributed to any one author.

editorialDecl.p: A formula is an attested conventional expression or recognisable adaptable pattern that performs a communicative function within colophon-writing. Recurrent vocabulary alone is insufficient. Assess evidence of conventionality separately from speech-act function: a unique assertion or prayer is not automatically a formula. An expression may be evidenced by independent corpus occurrences or relevant comparative scholarship; copied witnesses of one text are not independent evidence of recurrence.

Adaptation is permitted, not required: unchanged reproduction can remain formulaic. Formula boundaries follow meaningful pragmatic units, not fixed word counts, verse lengths, or identical wording. Dependent elements such as an address to the reader normally remain within the larger formula. No dedicated collocation tagging is required.

Tag formulae in the Armenian transcription only. Use seg/@type="formula" and seg/@ana, for example ../indices/listformula.xml#dir-remembrance-prayer-pattern-02. The nested categories record its subcategory and speech-act class; do not repeat those parent pointers. No local xml:id is required on a formula segment.

Use the most suitable functional unit without splitting it merely because it names a person, place, date, or role. Contributor identification, dates, and places are included in production and completion when part of that statement. Commissioning and sponsorship requires an explicit claim of requesting, financing, or supporting production; a name or honorific alone is insufficient. People, places, works, and contextual roles retain their own tagging inside the segment.

Classify petitions involving God or saints as expressives according to the project adaptation of Hjälm and Tarras; requests for human action are directives. Determine the intended actor and contextual force, not the grammatical imperative alone. Praise and thanksgiving can overlap with acknowledgement of divine assistance. Humility includes inadequacy and apology. An explicit appeal to a reader to forgive errors may also have directive force; no unagreed apology subcategory is introduced here.

Correction actively requests amendment of errors. Restraint in alteration discourages unwarranted textual change. Care and custody concerns physical handling, retention, lending, access, and use. These remain separate directive subcategories. Remembrance and prayer is a single merged category for human-directed remembrance and intercession.

Multiple classifications are permitted for a cohesive unit that performs overlapping functions. Space-separated ana pointers mean simultaneous analytical assignments, not mutually exclusive alternatives. Split successive acts where boundaries are clear; use multiple pointers where the same unit performs both.
Mortality and the endurance of writing is provisionally grouped under expressives.

A book curse is classified by its claimed performative sanction, not by a judgement that it had supernatural effect. Distinguish pronouncing an anathema from directing a reader not to remove a book or reporting an earlier donation. Constitutive dedication and custody provisions have not been added as a separate declarative subcategory; assess actual cases before expanding the inventory.

taxonomy.desc: Project classification: four parent classes with 4 assertive, 9 expressive, 4 directive, and 1 declarative subcategories. Labels and definitions are initial editorial decisions, to be refined against Armenian evidence. Standard patterns are nested within their subcategories; occurrence descriptions list the supplied Armenian passages with source pointers.

category.catDesc: Presents information as being the case; classification does not guarantee the historical truth of the assertion.

Records copying, making, or completing a manuscript or textual unit, including identification of those responsible and contextual dates and places. Illustrative English example: This Gospel was completed by Aharovn in Alexandria.

category.n: Writing dated and attributed to a scribe
category.catDesc: States that a sacred text was written in a specified year by the hand of a named scribe.
col-000001, col-000001-wit-000001: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fol. 278v: ի թուականութեանն Հայոց ՇԽԸ գրեցաւ սուրբ [Աւ]ետարանս ձեռամբ Ահարովնի

category.n: Writing situated under ecclesiastical and political authorities
category.catDesc: Situates the writing of a sacred text within the tenure of named ecclesiastical and political authorities.

col-000001, col-000001-wit-000001: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fol. 279v: Արդ գրեցաւ սուրբ Աւետարանս ի հայրապետութեանն տեառն Գրիգորի և յինքնակալնութեանն Հռոմայեացւոցն ազգին արիական որ են փառանգս

category.n: Completion in a named place under saintly protection
category.catDesc: Records completion of a sacred text in a named place, with saintly protection and a Christological closing phrase.

col-000001, col-000001-wit-000001: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fol. 280r: աւարտեցաւ սուրբ Աւետարանս ի մայրաքաղաք Աղեկսանդրու ընդ հովանե[ա]ւ Յովհաննու աւետարանչին ի Քրիստոս Յիսուս ի Տեր,

Explicitly records a request, financing, or other support for production; do not infer it from a named person alone. Illustrative English example: This book was written at the request and expense of its patron.

Records exemplars, translation, collation, revision, or correction. Reports performed textual work rather than asking a future reader to perform it. Illustrative English example: I translated this work and checked it against another exemplar.

category.n: Translation from Greek into Armenian with place and date
category.catDesc: Records translation of a martyrdom account from Greek into Armenian, identifying the place and year. Singular and plural wording, spelling, and numeral notation are recorded as witness variants of this pattern.

col-000002, col-000002-wit-000001: Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, MS. Arménien 178, fol. 209r: Թարգմանեցաւ պատմութիւն սրբոց վկայիցս ի յունարէն գրոց ի հայերեն բարբառ: ի մայրաքաղաքին Հայոց որ կոչի Մելետինի: Ի թուականիս ի հինգ հարիւր քառասուն և մի:

col-000002, col-000002-wit-000002: Venice, Mekhitarist monastery of San Lazzaro MS. 17, fol. 202v: Թարգմանեցան պատմութիւնք գրոց սրբոց վկայիցս ի յունարէն ի հայ բարբար: ի մայրաքաղաքին Հայոց որ կոչի Մելիտինի: Ի թուականիս Հայոց ՇԽԱ:

col-000002, col-000002-wit-000003: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 6196, fol. 239v: Թարգմանեցան պատմութիւնք սրբոց վկայիցս ի յունարէն գրոց ի հայ բարբար: ի մայրաքաղաքին Հայոց որ կոչի Մելետենի: Ի թուականիս Հայոց հինգ հարիւր և քառասուն և մեկ:
Records possession, acquisition, donation, or a change in custody, without automatically creating an event record. Illustrative English example: I acquired this book and gave it to the monastery.
Expresses attitudes, feelings, or wishes, including divine-directed petitions under the project convention.
Offers glory or praise to God; distinguish praise offered from an instruction to a human audience to praise. Illustrative English example: Glory to the holy Trinity.

category.n: Praise of the Trinity through divine attributes
category.catDesc: Offers glory to the Trinity through a sequence of divine attributes.
col-000001, col-000001-wit-000001: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fol. 278v: Փառք երից անբաւից կարելեաց անկարից եռանձնե[այ] միութեան իսկունականաց
Offers enduring glory to the divine recipient, using a relative clause or direct address and closing with Amen.
col-000001, col-000001-wit-000001: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fol. 280r: որում փառք [աւ]իտեանս ամէն:
col-000001, col-000001-wit-000001: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fol. 280v: և քեզ փառք յաւիտեանս ամէն
Affirms or wishes perpetual blessedness for the divine recipient and closes with Amen; grammatical differences between witnesses remain within this provisional pattern.
col-000002, col-000002-wit-000001: Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, MS. Arménien 178, fol. 209r: ինքն եղիցի աւրհնեալ յաւիտեանս: Ամէն:
col-000002, col-000002-wit-000003: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 6196, fol. 239v: այն որ միշտ աւրհնեալ է յաւիտեանս յաւիտենից: Ամեն:
Expresses gratitude, especially for successful completion. Illustrative English example: Thanks be to God who enabled its completion.

Recognises divine help in beginning, carrying out, or completing the work; may overlap with thanksgiving or assertive production. Illustrative English example: With God’s assistance I reached the end.

Formulaic expressions of unworthiness, sinfulness, deficient skill, or other limitations, including apologies for faults in the work. Illustrative English example: I, the unworthy and ignorant scribe, regret the faults in my writing.
Describes the scribe through expressions of deficient ability and monastic unworthiness.
col-000001, col-000001-wit-000001: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fol. 278v: ախմարի և փանաքի գրչի և անպիտան կրաւնաւորի
Expresses effort, suffering, or difficult conditions associated with writing. Illustrative English example: My hand laboured and my whole body suffered.
Expresses satisfaction or relief on finishing the work, including conventional comparisons. Illustrative English example: As a traveller rejoices at homecoming, so does the scribe at completion.

Petitions God for mercy or remission of sins. A request that a human reader pray for forgiveness belongs to remembrance and prayer. Illustrative English example: May God forgive those who wrote this book.

category.n: Wish for divine mercy upon the audience
category.catDesc: Wishes divine mercy upon the addressees; differences in the extent of the audience do not create a new pattern.
col-000001, col-000001-wit-000001: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fol. 279r: և Աստուած ձեզ ողորմեսցի ամէն·
col-000001, col-000001-wit-000001: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fol. 279r: և Աստուած ամենեցուն ողորմեսցի ամէն·

category.n: Mercy, erasure of sins, and inscription in the Book of Life
category.catDesc: Petitions for mercy upon a named soul through saintly intercession, erasure of the record of sins, and inscription in the Book of Life.

col-000001, col-000001-wit-000001: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fol. 279r: և Քրիստոս Աստուած այս սուրբ Աւետարանչացս բարէխաւսութեամբ և սուրբ Աստուածածին և սուրբ Կարապետն բարէխաւսութեամբ ողորմեսցի Յովհաննիսի հոգւոյն և ջնջեսցէ զձեռագիր յանցանաց նորա և գրեսց[է] ի դպրութիւն կենաց ամէն

category.n: Personal plea for mercy and forgiveness
category.catDesc: The speaker petitions God for mercy in distress and forgiveness of sins, invoking divine ability.

col-000001, col-000001-wit-000001: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fol. 280v: Տէր Աստուած ողորմեա նեղացելոյս Ահարոնի շնորհեա իմ բազում մեղացն թողութիւն զի դու կարող ես ամենայնի,

category.n: Mercy for a named beneficiary through saintly prayers
category.catDesc: Invokes the saints’ prayers and asks Christ God for mercy upon a named beneficiary. Names and contextual roles are variable.
col-000002, col-000002-wit-000003: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 6196, fol. 239v: Աղաւթիւք սրբոցս ողորմեա Քրիստոս Աստուած Վարդան վարդապետ եւ ստացող ի գրոցս: Ամեն:
Wishes or petitions for divine blessing, protection, or reward, including through saintly intercession. Remembrance formulae belong to the remembrance and prayer category.

category.n: Reward for those involved in the text
category.catDesc: Wishes a divine reward through the martyrs’ intercession for the translator, scribe, and others involved in producing or receiving the text. The beneficiaries vary between witnesses.

col-000002, col-000002-wit-000001: Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, MS. Arménien 178, fol. 209r: Ընդ որս և Քրիստոս բարեխաւսութեամբ սուրբ վկայից տացէ վարձս թարգմանողին և գրուղին աշխատելոց ի սմա, ընթերցաւղաց եւ լսաւղաց եւ ստացաւղաց եւ

col-000002, col-000002-wit-000003: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 6196, fol. 239v: Ընդ որս և Քրիստոս բարեխաւսութեամբ սրբոցս տացէ վարձս բարեաց թարգմանչի և գրչի եւ ամենայն աշխատելոցս ի սմա բանիւ շարադրելոյ եւ գրչի գրելոյ

category.n: Mortality and the endurance of writing
category.catDesc: Conventionally reflects on the contrast between the mortal writer and surviving text. Placement under expressive is provisional; assess contextual assertive force. Illustrative English example: The hand will perish, but the writing remains.
Seeks an action or restraint from a human recipient, including an implied future reader.

Requests human recipients to remember someone, pray for them, or commemorate them in prayer. Remembrance and memorial intercession are merged here. Reciprocal remembrance is also grouped here by project convention. Illustrative English example: Remember us in your holy prayers.

category.n: Request that readers pray for the speaker
category.catDesc: Appeals to those who benefit from the sacred text to include the speaker in their prayers.

col-000001, col-000001-wit-000001: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fol. 279r: Արդ աղաչեմ զամենեսին որք լուսաւորիք և աւգտիք ի սուրբ Աւետարանիդ զիս աղաւթից արժան արասջիք

category.n: Remember a named person in holy prayers
category.catDesc: Requests remembrance of a named beneficiary in the recipients’ holy prayers. The beneficiary’s name is variable.
col-000001, col-000001-wit-000001: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fol. 279r: Արդ աղաչեմ զամենեսեան յիշեցէք ի ձեր սուրբ աղաւթս զՅովհաննէս
Wishes that those who remember will themselves be remembered.
col-000001, col-000001-wit-000001: Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fol. 279r: եւ որ յիշէք յիշել լիցիք
Requests amendment of textual or scribal errors. Illustrative English example: Correct whatever you find mistaken.
Requests avoidance of unwarranted changes to the text; distinct from an invitation to correct errors. Illustrative English example: Do not alter this text carelessly.
Instructs recipients how to handle, preserve, retain, lend, or use the book. Illustrative English example: Keep this book here and handle it carefully.
Claims to impose a sanction through the pronouncement itself; the classification describes claimed force, not demonstrated effect.

Pronounces sanctions against prohibited actions affecting the book, including removal, disposal, damage, or alteration. Illustrative English example: Whoever removes this book shall be under anathema.

revisionDesc.change: Added sixteen standard patterns using the IDs in col-000001 and col-000002, with all twenty-two supplied Armenian occurrences listed under their patterns. Updated the policy and templates to use direct pattern pointers in Armenian transcriptions.
Created the initial formula classification: four parent classes and eighteen subcategories.

body.p: Formula classifications, patterns, and occurrences are recorded in the header.
